raw_inputs.population_services_boundary: Disruptions affect economies, information access, public services and the daily lives of billions; no precise affected-person count is asserted.
raw_inputs.evidence_boundary: Global cable faults quantify network burden but are not silently relabeled as landing-point failures or full service outages.

transformations.formula: Normalize the upper bound of the ITU global annual cable-fault range against declared anchors.
Normalize the source-reported share of international data traffic carried by submarine cables.
Use the assessment decade as a conservative persistence interval; do not convert faults into outage-hours.
Assign full extent because the reported network, traffic and fault totals are worldwide.

receipts.uncertainty: Cable-system and fault totals are rounded global infrastructure statistics, and a cable fault is not necessarily a service outage at a landing point. Arctic ship counts cover the IMO Polar Code area; unique ships, aggregate distance and ship-type growth are retained as separate measures.
receipts.freshness: ITU global infrastructure assessment for 2025; snapshot captured 2026-08-01T00:00:00.000Z.

selection_reason.selected_method_passed: ITU quantifies global annual fault burden, international traffic dependence, persistent infrastructure exposure and worldwide extent.
higher_priority_failures: No globally harmonized current landing-point outage series supplies magnitude plus threshold or momentum at the required coverage.
